title: An exact 10-year decay clock leaves a 72.3 umol/kg oxygen-use gap in a 2021 age-mixture test with uncertain use curves
abstract: We tested whether tracer measurements resolve oxygen use when its age curve is uncertain. We used 2021.5 atmospheric CFC-12 and SF6 histories, ages from zero to 100 years, and a 90 umol/kg oxygen-use scale. The common law is any positive mixture of curves that rise linearly until an age from 1 to 30 years and then stop. The worst gap over this entire family reduces to scalar ramp tests. Two constructed spectra share exact CFC-12, SF6 and an ideal 10-year decay value but differ in AOU by 72.313 umol/kg under one unchanged law. At 0.5% source-normalized error, adding 1- and 3-year clocks bounds the worst family gap by 23.92-24.80 umol/kg, versus 79.77-80.43 for a 10-year clock. The pair is best among six candidate pairs at all three tested error levels. Excluding rapid early use reverses some rankings. Continuous-age and continuous-shape bounds, 7,953 dual checks, primal witnesses and a grid repeat support the comparison. These are global information limits with ideal measurements and constructed spectra, not field uncertainty intervals or attribution of the California oxygen loss. Unknown source properties, path-dependent respiration and transport remain outside the model.

display.caption: Worst oxygen-use gaps in a 2021 constructed age-mixture test. The left panel varies the use curve. The right panel bounds all positive mixtures of the tested continuous curve family. All designs include CFC-12 and SF6. Ideal clock labels are e-folding times in years. The error is 0.5% of the contemporary source value. These are model bounds, not ocean observations.
